clue.text: Looter found lots of beer, and more besides

indicators.note: lots of a thing is most of it, so the beer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Pils is a pale beer, short for Pilsener
more beer besides, here lager

explanation.surface: A looter breaks into an off-licence and finds crates of beer and plenty else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots of' trims PILS to PIL; 'and more besides' adds a second beer, LAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillager is one who plunders, a direct synonym for a looter.

clue.text: A fraction indecent?

parts.note: a top-heavy fraction like seven over four has a name that also means rude or unseemly

explanation.surface: Asking whether a number could be rude.
explanation.definitionFit: An improper fraction has a numerator larger than its denominator; improper also means indecent.

clue.text: Take off after end of flight here?

definitions.text: Take off after end of flight here?

indicators.note: after places the removal of clothes behind the end of flight

parts.note: landing ends a flight
strip means take off clothes

explanation.surface: Where a plane takes off again after landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' reads as an aircraft leaving, but it means undress; the whole clue also describes a runway.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip is a basic runway where aircraft land and take off.

clue.text: Underdog unfortunately prevented from leaving home

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters of Underdog are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The underdog is unluckily kept indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounded child is punished by being forbidden to go out.

clue.text: US agent, given a pile, having change of heart

indicators.note: heart is the central letter, and change swaps it for another

parts.note: an atomic pile is a nuclear reactor

explanation.surface: An American estate agent, offered a fortune, has second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having change of heart' swaps the middle C of REACTOR for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Realtor is the American word for an estate agent.

clue.text: Perhaps does put up with it and make more changes

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means written bottom to top, reversing the word

parts.note: does are female deer, so they are an example of deer

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates it and keeps revising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' reads as tolerate; 'put up' reverses DEER to REED and 'with' joins IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-edit is to edit again, making further changes to a text.

clue.text: Largely tasteless food

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: tacky means vulgar or tasteless

explanation.surface: Most of the food is bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tasteless' suggests bland food, but here it means vulgar: TACKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tack is slang for food, as in hard tack, the ship's biscuit.

clue.text: Member of film crew finishes 'musical clip

indicators.note: finishes means comes at the end, so the crew member follows the musical

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a grip is a film technician who handles camera rigs

explanation.surface: A film technician wraps up a short excerpt from a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clip' reads as a film excerpt, fitting the scene; it is the definition, a hair clip.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairgrip is a small sprung clip that holds hair in place.

clue.text: Beastly group thus bidding farewell to paradise?

indicators.note: to here means attached after, so the farewell follows paradise

parts.note: Eden is the biblical paradise
ta-ta is a casual goodbye

explanation.surface: Someone leaving paradise waves goodbye, as Adam and Eve did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' says the answer read in two parts acts out the phrase: paradise, ta-ta.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentata is the zoological order of toothless mammals such as sloths and anteaters, a group of beasts.

clue.text: Bridge partners entertaining the old man

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold as a guest, so the partners hold the father between them

parts.note: in bridge North and South play as partners
the old man is slang for father, PA

explanation.surface: Two bridge players have one of their fathers round to the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like part of 'Bridge partners', but it is the definition alone; the partners are North and South.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the arch or stretch of a bridge between supports, and a verb meaning to bridge.

clue.text: Bus turned back sharply near rocky creek

parts.note: to double back is to turn sharply and retrace your route

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of creek are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A bus makes a sharp U-turn beside a stony stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back sharply' looks like a description of the bus's manoeuvre, but it is a single synonym; 'rocky' shuffles the creek's letters and 'near' simply places them alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-decker is a bus with two passenger levels, familiar in London.

clue.text: Joining together Lancashire and Cheshire, you might say, is mean

indicators.note: you might say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Lancashire and Cheshire are both English cheeses, and joining them together is pairing

explanation.surface: Merging two neighbouring English counties is called stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire and Cheshire look like counties, but here they are cheeses, paired.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeseparing means stingy, as if paring rind off cheese to save every scrap.

clue.text: Thought nothing should get wasted

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to pine is to waste away, so pined means got wasted

explanation.surface: Advice that nothing ought to go to waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state a view, so opined is a past-tense synonym of thought.

clue.text: Another upset about independent broadcasting

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the single letter
upset means knocked over, so the letters of Another are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: More turmoil over an independent broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ANOTHER into ONTHEAR, and 'about' wraps it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on the air is being broadcast at that moment, so the phrase equals broadcasting.

clue.text: Salvation Army is drawn into vulgar religious campaign

indicators.note: being drawn into something means going inside it, so the army goes inside the vulgar word

parts.note: crude means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army gets dragged into a coarse campaign of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crusades were medieval religious wars, and a crusade is any campaign pursued with zeal.

clue.text: Neat and tidy sums to be made from these business enterprises?

parts.note: a tidy sum is a lot of money, cash
neat is an old word for cattle, so cows

explanation.surface: Ventures expected to yield neat profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as tidy, but it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business enterprise that steadily generates profit.

clue.text: Picture how a business might cease trading

definitions.meaning: a photograph taken at short range

definitions.text: how a business might cease trading
definitions.meaning: a shop might ... when it shuts for good

explanation.surface: A snapshot of a firm closing its doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-up is a photograph at short range; close up is a verb phrase for a business shutting down.

clue.text: Spot about to be covered by antiseptic liquid

indicators.note: covered by means sitting inside, so the short word for about goes in the liquid

parts.note: a lotion is a soothing liquid for the skin
CA, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A pimple is about to be dabbed with antiseptic lotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' reads as a pimple, but it means a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A location is a place or position, the same as a spot.

clue.text: Ran after 'ound, getting lost

indicators.note: after places the word for ran behind the Cockney hunt

parts.note: to hound is to hunt; the dropped h of the clue is dropped from hunt too
raced means ran

explanation.surface: A Cockney chased after a hound and lost his way.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ound' shows a dropped H, so the synonym HUNT loses its H as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Untraced means not found, so lost.

clue.text: Breather needed at home to get healthier

parts.note: in means at home
hale means healthy, so haler is healthier

explanation.surface: To feel better, you need a rest at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' reads as a rest, but it is a device you breathe from.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is a device through which you breathe medicine, so a breather in a punning sense.

clue.text: Novel delivered by an author

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's novel
rid means freed or delivered from

explanation.surface: A new book handed over by its writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' wants to be an anagram signal; it is the title of a book, She.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Brinsley Sheridan was an Irish playwright, the writer of The School for Scandal.

clue.text: "Boy meets girl" is the set-up in this former TV series

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means each word written bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Boy meets girl is the premise of an old television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' reads as the premise, but it turns LAD and SAL upward to DAL and LAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas was a long-running American TV soap about an oil-rich Texan family.

clue.text: Get it 'with a glass of sherry

parts.note: cop it is British slang for get punished, get it in the neck

explanation.surface: Someone is told off and then handed a drink of sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: A copita is the tulip-shaped glass used for sherry in Spain, and a glass of sherry served in it.

clue.text: Psalm teacher, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A guess at the job of someone who teaches psalms.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the anagram of PSALM TEACHER describes someone who might teach psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapelmaster directs the music of a chapel choir, which would include teaching psalms.

clue.text: Display on English river

indicators.note: on in a down clue places one piece above the other

parts.note: to air is to display or show

explanation.surface: A show held on the banks of an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England, flowing through Leeds.

clue.text: Child's attachment to computer technology is a source of irritation

indicators.note: an attachment to something is added on the end, so the child's letters follow

parts.note: IT stands for information technology
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A child glued to a computer drives the grown-ups mad.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a skin irritation, and anything that nags at you.

clue.text: Fighter needed map, entering town in Herts

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the map goes inside the town

parts.note: Ware is a town in Hertfordshire, an English county north of London
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot needed a map to find a small town in Hertfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A warplane is a military aircraft, and a fighter is one kind.

clue.text: Frenchman's right out of step, being a deserter

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: out of means leaving, so the letter for right leaves the step

parts.note: a grade is a step on a scale

explanation.surface: A French soldier out of step with his unit turns out to be a deserter.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade abandons a cause or side, much as a deserter abandons the army.
